correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly gives the dimension, field, update and T/p quantifiers. A^2=(d mod 2)I follows from commuting coordinate flips; rank-half identities from a block involution. The invariant four-space W has an explicit B action. Even d: companion factor (X^2+X+1)^2 and m-2 nilpotent J2 blocks follow from exact ranks B=m+2 and B^2=4. Odd d: kerB is a semisimple two-space; exact ranks of (B+I), (B+I)^2 and (B+I)^3 yield one J4(1) plus m-3 J2(1) blocks. Fitting and fixed-space counts yield the stated orbit and entry-time formulas. Standalone verification of 98 finite rank profiles and 131600 configurations across two finite fields passed, but finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The even-dimensional Jordan form is algebraically identical to the prior adjacent two-site diagonal feedback classification and is explicitly acknowledged as covered at the similarity-class level. The new graph-edge deletion problem is not the same update; in odd dimension its zero-primary block is J1(0)^2 instead of the earlier feedback J2(0), a genuine new stopping-time and semisimplicity distinction. The full edge-deletion theorem is proved directly and compared with material primary articles on hypercube automata, one-dimensional linear CA and real spectral edge faults, and six actual research-record queries. Residual unindexed-history risk remains.
residual_risks: The even-dimensional similarity class is already present in the accessible adjacent two-site feedback result; standalone novelty rests on identifying the missing-bond update and its odd-dimensional different nilpotent kernel, not on its even-dimensional orbit formula.
An unindexed paper on modular adjacency ranks of an edge-faulty hypercube could subsume the asserted result without appearing in searched indexes.

value.rationale: A single missing interconnection is a canonical network perturbation. Its all-dimensional parity classification supplies a meaningful structural contrast with adjacent two-site self-feedback: identical finite dynamics up to linear conjugacy in even dimension, identical persistent cycle structure but different semisimplicity and transient horizons in odd dimension. Exact populations for the missing-bond operator and a sharp universal one-step odd-dimensional law are natural dynamical invariants, though the even-dimensional similarity type alone is already known from the prior paired-feedback result.
